# What the Toys Cannot Show {#sec-toy-limits}

Every result in this book is computed on a small synthetic testbed whose truth is known
exactly ([The Testbeds](appendix-testbeds.qmd#sec-testbeds)). That is what makes the results
checkable, and it is also their limit: a toy shows a mechanism and its direction, not its size
on real data. Each chapter ends by saying what its toy cannot show. This appendix collects
those sections, generated from the chapters, so the limits can be read in one place.

Four limits recur:

- **Scale.** The testbeds have a few dimensions and thousands of examples; the reported
  large-scale results are stated from their sources, not reproduced.
- **Real data.** Real missingness, noise, shift and duplication mix mechanisms that a testbed
  isolates one at a time, and which mechanism holds is often not testable from the data.
- **Real models.** Most demonstrations use linear models, a memorizer or a bigram model; how
  much a flexible model is affected is not measured here.
- **Estimated, not known, quantities.** The testbeds give exact margins, posteriors, density
  ratios and floors; practice has to estimate them, and the estimates carry their own error.
